text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty INC-7521 triggered — elevated 503s for /v1/generate across west1 (error rate ~18% last 5m). Alerting oncall.

Leah: I'm on for the next 8m and then I have to step out. Handing off now — need a driver and a comms owner. Current impact: customer-facing latency and some 503s, severity P1. Logs show backend model pool returning 503s when requests hit a specific GPU node.

Leah: Marco — you’re incoming in ~10m. Can you take driver? Jia can you own external comms?

Marco: I can take driver now if needed, I'm by my laptop. I'll shadow for the handoff and then take full ownership.

Jia: I can handle comms. I'll prepare a short public/status draft and post to #status when we confirm root cause.

Sam: Quick checks before we escalate:
- run `curl -sS https://metrics.internal/recent?svc=inference | jq '.errors["/v1/generate"]'`
- check node health: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-west1`
- look at gateway logs `gcloud logging read \"resource.type=gae_app AND severity>=ERROR AND textPayload:503\" --limit 50`

Priya: I'm on standby for a possible rollback to a recent model snapshot if the node-level issues persist. If driver requests, I can trigger the fallback variant.

Leah: Repo runbook link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/inference-503. Relevant excerpt: 
```
If 503s concentrated in single AZ:
 1) Move traffic to healthy AZs via router reroute `infra-router shift --from=west1 --to=west2 --weight=0.8`
 2) Scale up dedicated pool in west1 (short-term) `dedicatedctl scale --pool inference-west1 --replicas 4`
 3) If node-level NG, cordon & restart: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl delete pod <pod>`
 4) If model process crashing, fallback to quantized-variant: update route mapping
```

Marco: Running the first checks now. `kubectl get pods -n inference -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount}' | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -nr | head -n 5` shows a couple pods with restartCount > 3 in gpu-west1. Also seeing OOM-ish traces in the logs: `OOMKilled` for pod inference-worker-7.

Marco: K8s suggests node gpu-west1-3 has been flapping. I'm going to cordon it and spin up replacements. Doing: `kubectl cordon gpu-west1-3` and `kubectl delete pod inference-worker-7` now.

ops-bot: Action accepted — cordon request queued. Autoscaler will provision replacement nodes if cluster has capacity.

Jia: Draft status (short): 
> We are investigating elevated 503 errors for Redwood inference in west1. Engineers are rerouting traffic and replacing unstable nodes. Some customers may experience degraded responses. We'll post updates every 10 minutes.

Sam: While cordoning, let's also open temporary routing to west2 to reduce customer impact. Marco — can you execute a weight shift of 30% in the router? Command: `infra-router shift --from=west1 --to=west2 --weight=0.3`

Marco: Running the shift now. `infra-router` output: `{\"result\":\"ok\", \"applied\": {\"west2\": 0.3}}`. Monitoring traffic after shift.

Leah: Jia — post the draft to #status with incident tag and link to the runbook. Add note: "We will update within 10 minutes".

Jia: Posted to #status and sent short ping to customer success for major accounts. :thumbsup:

Marco: Node replacements provisioning. New pods coming up, but I still see a spike of 503s for a few in-flight requests. Error logs show `model-serving: kv-cache-miss` correlated with crash windows. Could be a memory leak in our cache layer.

Priya: If it's cache-related we can temporarily disable large prefix caching for the affected route: `service-config set /v1/generate --param cache_prefix_size=0` — this will increase per-token compute but reduce memory pressure. Should I flip it?

Marco: Do it. Flipping now.

ops-bot: config update accepted for /v1/generate by Priya. Rolling update to routes in west1.

Marco: Cache disabling applied. Error rate down from 18% -> 6% in the last 3m. Pod restarts leveling off.

Leah: Great — Marco is driving, Jia is comms, Priya on config changes, Sam on monitoring. I'm assigning myself as backup and will stay reachable by DM for another 5m, then hand off fully.

Jia: Update posted to #status: majority of customers seeing reduced errors; working on full remediation.

Sam: Recommend keeping router shift in place until new nodes are stable for 20 minutes and error rate <1% for 10m. Also open a follow-up ticket for a deep-dive into kv-cache memory usage.

Marco: Agreed. I'll keep driver until nodes are all healthy. I'll also collect kube-dump and heap profiles: `kubectl exec -n inference <pod> -- pmap -x` and upload to /tmp/incident/1765439999 for investigation.

Leah: Handoff note: Marco (driver), Jia (comms). If anything shifts back up, tag @Leah and escalate to oncall-senior.

Jia: Will do. Sending final update to customers: reduced impact, mitigation in place, next update in 20m.

Priya: Leaving a quick postmortem checklist in the ticket: restart counts, node flapping times, cache param flip, routing shift windows, and heap dumps.

incident-bot: Incident INC-7521 marked as "mitigated" by Marco at 1765441180. Please create follow-up incident review within 48h.

Marco: Confirmed mitigated. I'll file the incident review with timeline and artifacts. Thanks team. :clap:
